# v0.16.24 — Prelaunch scope recovery

## Changes

- Recover an operation rejected before launch after an effective scope correction, while recording call-, run- and input-bound host receipts and preventing duplicate admission.
- Reconcile native history, including concurrent status reads, unavailable history and contradictory process evidence, without treating a tool envelope or error text as proof that a process started or did not start.
- Resolve a limited initial prefix of immutable PowerShell path definitions without evaluating expressions. Preserve literal-dollar paths and reject unresolved destinations after pipelines, executable prefixes or engine-owned variable assignments.
- Bind the isolated prelaunch-recovery CLI scenario to its actual direct root executor and model; a Worker dispatch is not accepted as that scenario's direct execution.

These changes do not recover another owner's live operation or establish completion or grading of an external task.

## Release identity and validation

The intended runtime asset marker is `0.16.24-prelaunch-scope-recovery-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and SHA-256-pinned archive alongside candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI, independent review, and actual CLI Worker startup. Startup is not task completion or an official score. Install and publish the same fixed archive. An installed marker does not prove that a running OpenCode host has reloaded the plugin; verify its loaded path and marker after a manual restart.

# v0.16.23 — Timed operation boundary correction

## Changes

- Reject additional shell commands and input redirections appended to a declared timed operation, including LF and CRLF boundaries. This corrects an operation-observation gap in v0.16.22.
- Preserve existing matching for valid timed operations, declared redirects, failure results, and observation ownership. The fix covers the public Mission tool hook and both plain and explicitly timed declarations.
- The change does not recover uncollected operations from other owners or runs and does not establish recovery of the original live operation.

## Release identity and validation

The intended runtime asset marker is `0.16.23-operation-boundary-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and SHA-256-pinned archive alongside candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI, and actual CLI Worker startup. Startup is not task completion or an official score. Install and publish the same fixed archive. An installed marker does not prove that a running OpenCode host has reloaded the plugin; verify its loaded path and marker after a manual restart.

releases.name: v0.16.22 — Timed operation observation
releases.body:
# v0.16.22 — Timed operation observation

## Changes

- Recognize the literal POSIX `TIMEFORMAT='<ASCII_IDENTIFIER>=%R'; time <command>` envelope when reconciling a native operation, without accepting a different command, output redirection, working directory or arbitrary shell wrapper.
- Retain an already collected operation observation across a unique equivalent declaration in the same working directory. Original ownership, terminal and exit remain attached to the observation; a bare Node declaration cannot prove that a different pinned binary ran.
- Classify `NO_START` and structured failure output separately from the recognized envelope's trailing duration, without changing the native output or exit.
- The change does not import an uncollected call from another owner or run, and does not establish recovery of the original live operation. The regression tests cover the V2 history projection and public Mission APIs, not a replay of that operation.

## Release identity and validation

The intended runtime asset marker is `0.16.22-operation-elapsed-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and SHA-256-pinned archive with the candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI and actual CLI Worker startup separately; a startup is not completion or an official score. Use the same fixed archive for installation and publication. An installed marker does not prove that an already-running OpenCode host reloaded the plugin; verify the loaded path and marker after a manual restart.

releases.name: v0.16.21 — Narrow blocker-scope reconsideration
releases.body:
# v0.16.21 — Narrow blocker-scope reconsideration

## Changes

- A blocked submission or a question naming an explicitly stopped method can prompt one scope reconsideration when unmet work remains. The observation is not evidence of independence or permission to act.
- A separate, deliberately narrow question recognizer covers the reported Japanese three-item availability form only when the retained request explicitly places Windows smoke after release and the single running unit has the matching Linux implementation objective. Unknown, conflicting or current dependencies fall back to the existing question path.
- An immediately repeated identical answered native question or completed Scout investigation can reuse the retained result as information, not fresh evidence or approval.
- Future checks, prohibitions, holds, budget, ownership and license conditions remain in force. The change does not automatically establish semantic independence, solve a Mission, or prove an improvement with a real model.

## Release identity and validation

The intended runtime asset marker is `0.16.21-blocker-scope-v1`. Record the integrated `main` commit and SHA-256-pinned archive with the candidate preflight, full validation, Linux/Windows CI and actual CLI Worker startup separately; a startup is not completion or an official score. Use the same fixed archive for installation and publication. An installed marker does not prove that an already-running OpenCode host reloaded the plugin; verify the loaded path and marker after a manual restart.

releases.name: v0.16.20 — Mission vision in Grip decisions
releases.body:
# v0.16.20 — Mission vision in Grip decisions

- #365: show the desired outcome and its relation to the current decision, explicitly distinguishing AI synthesis from original request evidence.
- Preserve saved Grip offers across display languages, normal choices, consultation holds and native permission/budget boundaries.
- Retain newly supplied public continuation context before validating a Mission vision reference.
- #366: synchronize package/lock version, runtime marker, regression expectation and current installation guides.

## Fixed release identity

- Commit: `aa681b8edbe8d51e3799128802e53f2c801879b6`
- Archive: `sortie-dogs-0.16.20.tgz` (940125 bytes)
- SHA-256: `dad60548f5b22d7aa76a95e4978b0ad914aef9d3665fb7379f9c795d58f823fa`
- Runtime marker: `0.16.20-mission-vision-v1`

## Validation

- Candidate preflight passed on this archive: 8 assets and runtime marker matched.
- Final `npm run test:full`: 2658 PASS / 4 SKIP, 137 files, exit 0, 448.735 seconds including build.
- Linux and Windows CI passed on the release commit: https://github.com/zufall-upon/Sortie-dogs/actions/runs/42973530885
- Normal OpenCode 2.2.6 CLI started the real Worker `openai/gpt-6.1-terra#max` in 21.655 seconds, matching this archive. This is startup evidence, not external-task completion or an official benchmark score.
- Probe priced estimate: $0.0565288 plus 2 unpriced requests. This is not a complete invoice or the entire Mission cost.
- The same archive was applied to both existing npm-global prefixes and the config-local package; 271 files per install, 8 assets and existing model overrides matched.

Npm publication and registry distribution are recorded separately. The user explicitly invoked this release routine; no unattended publication automation was added. Publication acceptance does not imply immediate registry propagation, and no accepted version is republished.

The shared OpenCode host was not stopped or restarted. Installed version/marker/bytes do not prove that an already running host loaded them; confirm the loaded path, marker and hash after the user's manual restart.
